Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.

L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference

to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-

sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.

formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome

oral-bioavailability outcome.

records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: C50 reports essentially complete absorption of oxcarbazepine after a single oral radiolabeled dose in humans; oxcarbazepine shares the dibenzazepine carboxamide core with the query and supports a favorable intestinal absorption component.

L1/L2 records for structurally related or similarly neutral lipophilic drugs report high oral bioavailability: imipramine-N-oxide ~100% (C06/C21), thalidomide 80-100% (C15/C18), and tolfenamic acid ~91-126% (C04/C14/C24/C28).

L3 oral exposure records for dibenzazepine carboxamides show substantial systemic exposure after oral dosing (C29-C36, C38-C40), consistent with absorption, though they do not by themselves quantify absolute F.

C68 is the only L6 record directly involving carbamazepine; it reports that cimetidine increased carbamazepine and 10,11-epoxide half-life by 10-20%, indicating CYP-mediated metabolism but not quantifying first-pass loss or F; it does not provide affirmative evidence for F < 20%.

Other L6 hepatic clearance/metabolic stability records concern oxcarbazepine (C65/C69/C70/C74), cyproheptadine (C66/C71), tricyclic UGT substrates (C67), and BPCPU (C72/C73/C75/C76); none are carbamazepine-specific and none provide affirmative low-F evidence.
Poor solubility/dissolution records C45 and C51 concern other molecules and do not constitute affirmative threshold-relevant evidence for F < 20% in carbamazepine.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for carbamazepine itself is supplied.
No carbamazepine-specific hepatic clearance or first-pass extraction measurement is supplied; C68 reports only half-life modulation by cimetidine.
L6 records mostly concern oxcarbazepine, cyproheptadine, BPCPU, and other molecules, not carbamazepine.
No formulation, dose, fed/fasted, or sampling context for the query is supplied.
No carbamazepine-specific solubility or dissolution data are supplied; the unfavorable solubility prior is in silico only.

The high prediction based on close analog absorption (C50), high oral bioavailability analogs (C06/C21/C15/C18/C04/C14/C24/C28), oral exposure records (C29-C36/C38-C40), and the favorable physicochemical prior is maintained.
